title: Create mini-boilerplates: tiny Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server, and CLI examples demonstrating retries & streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Ship a set of minimal, opinionated starter templates (mini-boilerplates) for Redwood SDKs that demonstrate best-practice patterns for streaming, retries, reconnect/backpressure, and token-level cost controls across three runtimes: Next.js (TS), FastAPI (Python), and a Go HTTP server, plus a tiny CLI example. Each template must be under ~150 lines of code, include a short README, and a single-file runnable demo. Templates should be suitable for customers to copy/paste into a project or use as playgrounds in docs.
acceptance_criteria: Four unique starter templates committed to repo under /examples/mini-boilerplates with README and run instructions

Each template shows: a) streaming generation example with graceful cancellation, b) a retry wrapper demonstrating idempotency/timeout policies, c) token-cost awareness comments and an example of prefix caching header usage
Unit/integration smoke script for each template (CI job) that runs the sample with a sandbox API key and verifies stream semantics and retry backoff behavior
PR includes code comments explaining trade-offs: minimal deps vs ergonomics and production considerations
Docs team sign-off on README clarity and examples; at least one external developer reproduced example within 24 hours

Collect telemetry hooks (minimal) in examples to show token counts and latencies - Observability
decisions: Use a single small RetryPolicy abstraction exported in each language with the same semantic defaults (max_attempts=3, base_backoff=200ms, max_backoff=2s, retry_on=[5xx,429,network])
Streaming API examples will use chunked iteration rather than buffering entire responses to emphasize low-latency UX
Keep third-party deps to a minimum (no heavy frameworks beyond FastAPI/Next.js) to keep examples portable
Do not include SDK full installation in templates; link to SDK quickstart instead to avoid drift

Design (Evan Ross): add a tiny diagram in README showing stream lifecycle and cancel flow; keep UI minimal
